meaning:
ἀτιμία, -ας, ἡ
(ἄτιμος) [in LXX for כְּלִמָּה, קָלוֹן, etc. ;]
dishonour, disgrace: 1Co.11:14, 2Co.6:8; εἰς ἀ., Rom.9:21, 2Ti.2:20; ἐν ἀ., 1Co.15:43; κατ᾽ ἀ., 2Co.11:21; πάθη ἀτιμίας, base passions, Rom.1:26.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: For this reason, God gave them up to vile passions. For their women changed the natural function into that which is against nature.
Doesn’t even nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair, it is a dishonor to him?
by glory and dishonor, by evil report and good report; as deceivers, and yet true;
Now in a large house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of clay. Some are for honor, and some for dishonor.
